accepted.question_text: Let X be a smooth projective variety, fix numerical invariants such as rank and Chern classes, and let M be a moduli space of semistable vector bundles on X with those invariants. On the open subset of M that parametrizes stable vector bundles, what geometric or structural properties does the stratification by fixed Iitaka dimension of the vector bundle have?
accepted.context_brief: Iitaka-dimension stratification of stable bundles

evidence.quote: Question 1. What are the properties of the stratification of the open part of M parametrizing stable vector bundles obtained by loci of fixed Iitaka dimension?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a smooth projective variety with dim X > 1, and let M be a moduli space of semistable vector bundles or sheaves on X with fixed numerical invariants. In the properly semistable locus of M there are points corresponding to non-locally free sheaves. What is the best way to extend the definition of Iitaka dimension from vector bundles to this more general setting so that it meaningfully applies to such non-locally free sheaves?
accepted.context_brief: Iitaka dimension for non-locally free semistable sheaves

evidence.quote: Question 2. If dim X > 1, then in the properly semistable part of M there are points associated to non-locally free sheaves. What is the optimal adaptation of the definition of Iitaka dimension to this more general situation?

accepted.question_text: After extending Iitaka dimension to the properly semistable setting of sheaves on a smooth projective variety X, what geometric features does the resulting stratification of the subset of M parametrizing equivalence classes of properly semistable sheaves have when that subset is decomposed by loci of fixed Iitaka dimension?
accepted.context_brief: Stratification of properly semistable sheaves by Iitaka dimension

evidence.quote: Question 3. What are the geometric features of the stratification of the subset of M parametrizing equivalence classes of properly semistable sheaves on X obtained by loci of fixed Iitaka dimension?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a normal projective variety X that admits no Ulrich sheaf at all?
accepted.context_brief: Existence of normal varieties without Ulrich sheaves

evidence.quote: Question 4. Does there exist a normal variety X without Ulrich sheaves?

accepted.question_text: Which smooth projective varieties carry Ulrich bundles?
accepted.context_brief: Classification of smooth varieties with Ulrich bundles

evidence.quote: Question 5. Which smooth projective varieties carry Ulrich bundles?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a smooth connected n-dimensional manifold with n >= 2 such that h^i(O_X) = 0 for all 1 <= i <= n-1, and let A(X) denote the set of ample line bundles L on X satisfying h^i(L^\otimes t) = 0 for all integers t and all 1 <= i <= n-1. Under what conditions is A(X) nonempty, and what is the dimension of A(X)?
accepted.context_brief: When the ample-vanishing set A(X) exists

evidence.quote: Question 6. Under what conditions is A(X) nonempty? What is dim A(X)?

accepted.question_text: Fix a positive integer r, and let X be as above with a set A(X) of ample line bundles L satisfying h^i(L^\otimes t) = 0 for all integers t and all 1 <= i <= n-1. Let A(X, r) be the set of rank r vector bundles E on X such that h^i(E \otimes L^\otimes t) = 0 for all integers t, all 1 <= i <= n-1, and all L in A(X). What properties characterize the subset A(X, r)?
accepted.context_brief: Properties of the vanishing class A(X,r)

evidence.quote: Question 7. What are the properties of the subset A(X, r) of all rank r vector bundles E on X such that hi(E ⊗ L⊗t) = 0 for all t ∈ Z, all i = 1, . . . , n − 1 and all L ∈ A(X)?

accepted.question_text: For an n-dimensional complex manifold X, what properties characterize the class of weakly k-Buchsbaum vector bundles on X? In particular, how should one describe this class even in basic cases such as products of projective spaces like P^a x P^{n-a} and (P^1)^n?
accepted.context_brief: Characterization of weakly k-Buchsbaum bundles

evidence.quote: Question 8. What properties characterize the set of all weakly k-Buchsbaum vector bundles on a n-dimensional complex manifold X?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a complex projective manifold of dimension greater than one. Higgs bundles and coHiggs bundles are usually defined using a single Higgs field or coHiggs field. What is the optimal way to extend these notions so that one can work with r >= 2 fields at once, while imposing a suitable integrability condition such as f_i wedge f_j = 0 for all i and j?
accepted.context_brief: Multiple-field Higgs and coHiggs bundles

evidence.quote: Question 9. What are the optimal extensions of the concepts of Higgs and coHiggs bundles to include r fields in place of 1 in the case of manifolds of dimension greater than one?

accepted.question_text: Let X = P^{n_1} x ... x P^{n_k} with k >= 2 be a multiprojective space. How does changing the polarization affect the moduli space of low-rank coHiggs bundles on X?
accepted.context_brief: Polarization dependence of coHiggs moduli on multiprojective spaces

evidence.quote: Question 10. How is the moduli space of low rank coHiggs bundles on X affected by a change of polarization?

accepted.question_text: If X is a smooth connected projective curve, what is the relationship between Brill-Noether theory for line bundles on X and Brill-Noether theory for stable vector bundles of rank r >= 2 on X?
accepted.context_brief: Comparing rank-one and higher-rank Brill-Noether theory

evidence.quote: Question 11. What is the relation between the Brill–Noether theory for line bundles on X and the Brill–Noether theory for stable rank r ≥ 2 vector bundles on X?

accepted.question_text: Fix rank r = 2 and consider smooth projective curves of high genus. What is the relationship between Brill-Noether loci and loci defined by fixed Clifford index values for semistable rank-2 vector bundles?
accepted.context_brief: Brill-Noether loci versus fixed Clifford-index loci

evidence.quote: Question 12. Fix rank r = 2 and high genus. What is the relation between the Brill–Noether loci and the loci of fixed Clifford indices?

accepted.question_text: For genus-2 curves, what is the configuration of wall-crossing values, and what are the limiting moduli spaces as alpha approaches +infinity and as alpha approaches 0+, in the theory of alpha-semistable coherent systems and holomorphic triples of fixed numerical type?
accepted.context_brief: Wall structure for genus-2 coherent systems and triples

evidence.quote: Question 13. What is the configuration of walls and what are the limits to +∞ and to 0+ for genus 2 curves? (it should not depend on the genus 2 curve).

evidence.quote: Question 14. What assumptions in the case of a reducible curve imply a positive answer to Butler’s question?

evidence.quote: Question 15. What should be the axioms for a general theory of local characteristic classes of vector bundles around a contractible subvariety?

evidence.quote: Question 16. What are its admissible numerical values?

accepted.question_text: For a chosen local numerical invariant of vector bundles near a contractible subvariety, which admissible values are actually realized by some vector bundle?
accepted.context_brief: Existence for admissible local-invariant values

evidence.quote: Question 17. Which admissible values of the local invariant are realized by some vector bundle?

accepted.question_text: For a local neighborhood N of a subvariety Y and a chosen set of local numerical invariants, what is the moduli space of all vector bundles on N with those prescribed local numerical invariants?
accepted.context_brief: Moduli with prescribed local numerical invariants

evidence.quote: Question 18. What is the moduli space of all vector bundles on N with prescribed local numerical invariants?

accepted.question_text: Let Z_k = Tot(O_{P^1}(-k)). If (w, h) is an admissible pair of local numerical invariants satisfying the bounds in [BGK2, Cor. 2.18], does there exist a vector bundle E on Z_k with width w(E) = w and height h(E) = h?
accepted.context_brief: Realizing admissible width-height pairs on Z_k

evidence.quote: Question 19. Let (w, h) be admissible values of local invariants on Zk, that is, they satisfy the bounds of [BGK2, Cor. 2.18]. Does there exist a vector bundle E on Zk with (w(E), h(E)) = (w, h)?

accepted.question_text: Let W_1 = O_{P^1}(-1) ⊕ O_{P^1}(-1), W_2 = O_{P^1}(-2) ⊕ O_{P^1}(0), and W_3 = O_{P^1}(-3) ⊕ O_{P^1}(+1), the local Calabi-Yau threefold models that arise from contracting a rational curve on a Calabi-Yau threefold. What local invariants stratify the moduli of holomorphic vector bundles on such a space W_k into Hausdorff components in the analytic topology?
accepted.context_brief: Hausdorff-stratifying invariants on local Calabi-Yau threefolds

evidence.quote: Question 20. What local invariants stratify the moduli of holomorphic vector bundles on Wk for k ≥ 1 into Hausdorff components (in the analytic topology)?

accepted.question_text: Once suitable local invariants are found for the local Calabi-Yau threefolds W_k, can one construct a Hausdorff stratification of the moduli stack M_n(W_k) of holomorphic bundles E on W_k satisfying χ(ℓ, E) = n?
accepted.context_brief: Hausdorff stratification of M_n(W_k)

evidence.quote: Question 21. Construct a Hausdorff stratification of the moduli stack Mn(Wk) of holomorphic bundles on Wk with χ(ℓ, E) = n.

accepted.question_text: For vector bundles E on W_1, is every admissible value of h^1(W_1, End(E)) realized by some vector bundle E?
accepted.context_brief: Realizing admissible h^1(W1, End(E)) values

evidence.quote: Question 22. Is every admissible value of h1(W1, End(E)) realized by some vector bundle E?

accepted.question_text: Is the Atiyah-Jones conjecture true for every irrational complex surface?
accepted.context_brief: Atiyah-Jones conjecture for irrational surfaces

evidence.quote: Question 23. Is the Atiyah–Jones conjecture true for any irrational complex surface?

accepted.question_text: The paper proves a vanishing statement comparing the homology of a rank-2 bundle moduli space and the corresponding moduli stack for products of Pic-independent curves when c_2 is large. Does an analogous statement hold for every surface of general type?
accepted.context_brief: Extending the moduli-space versus stack comparison theorem

evidence.quote: Question 24. Does a generalization of Thm. 6.2 holds for any surface of general type?

accepted.question_text: For a complex surface X, what is the fundamental group of the moduli space of instantons on X, or equivalently of the corresponding moduli space of holomorphic bundles when one works through the Kobayashi-Hitchin correspondence?

evidence.quote: Question 25. What is the fundamental group of the moduli space of instantons (or holomorphic bundles) on X?
